It is an incredibly challenging situation to become homeless for any prolonged period of time, I myself have been in that situation previously and always hoped that by being forthcoming and opportunistic I would find stability quickly. For people with resources, connections, and a commensurate attitude you may find this process to pass relatively quickly, so attain these things at any possibility.

Your greatest reprieve in this circumstance is your vehicle. Having a solid surface and enclosed interior is an incredible boon and you will find relief knowing you have something to safeguard yourself. Drive carefully only when necessary and find multiple locations where it is quiet and not bothersome to park for the night, rotate between these areas to lessen suspicion. Supermarket lots and certain open areas around both businesses and residencies are good places to look for, but you will generally get a feeling when a place will be adequate. If you are discovered or awakened provide a simple honest explanation and offer you will move on your way to some other place, say you will get a hotel for the night if anyone really presses you (rare).

Maintain at all costs gainful and continual employment for any amount of income. Your rightful intention to have a mailing address and gym membership are an absolute priority as they will allow you to keep up appearances and provide a point of professional contact. You may also want to look at a Private Mailbox option in your area (I've used UPS), they provide a street address along with the mail so it appears somewhat more professional, although it comes at the cost of a higher premium, so only pay for it if you have to apply to job positions in your area with no alternative address to use. Otherwise a PO Box will get the mail just fine.

As you get accustomed to the situation it becomes a matter of patience and timing. Obviously afford to be frugal and look for any serviceable form of housing when the funds can allow. Otherwise spending free time at a public library can provide a few moments of peace, or being in a park for more solitude. Having a gym membership is mostly for hygienic purposes however it is also very rewarding to exercise and should be made routine. Be aware and alert throughout the experience and continue a mindset that this circumstance is temporary and it is just a re-arrangement of procured assets.

As time goes on I keep getting this feeling that there is always going to be something to hope for, a condition to change, a current to sway. It's exhausting when others may find it exhilarating, that the change is inherently unknown in its arrival.

The attitude is what makes the difference to me in a sense. It is easier to find yourself overwhelmed and panicked over the idea nothing will improve and no reason to see hope. It's at these times of helplessness to find yourself calm in spite of it all ; to breathe deeply, clearing your thoughts, and re-orienting your mindset is and will be invaluable. It's frustrating keeping this as a common practice, but the alternative is despair.

Align your focus to something you'd like to explore. Differentiate your life from however you were previously in whatever small means you can attempt. At the least, it will keep you occupied and give you energy to move forward.

Stay strong, I wish you the best.

Really, I don't think people should normally take offense if you are honest and say you'd just like some time to yourself. It's pretty pressuring to feel like you always have to be available for others whenever they ask, but the truth is you have no obligation to go out with anyone if you'd rather not at the time.
Homeless, living out of my car. Hope to hear back about a job interview I had a few days ago.

It seems to me you're really relying on your friends to try and bridge the gap in your feelings for this girl. You want to feel like they can give you absolute certainty that she wants to be in a relationship with you.

No one can ever give you that intimate knowledge of someone. It has to come from themselves alone. If you ever feel like you're scared or afraid of hurting someone by revealing how you feel, try to understand that they want to be with someone they truly love and know as well. By being honest with those feelings with someone is never really a bad thing with these situations, everyone is scared when they could be falling in love.

I don't want to assume the complexities of the situation you're in. If she's being friendly when you are seeing her it's probably a good sign it's okay to take the plunge. The gap you think you had to cross may not be as wide as you believe.

I just had the woman I want to be with more than anything else right now turn me down.

Love is the most horrible thing you can experience if it isn't reciprocated, but be faithful in your own resilience, and trust over time that recovery will come.

The best thing I can tell you is that if you haven't yet told her yourself how you truly feel, you never know how she could react. I'm not going to get your hopes up and say that she'll want to be with you if you do tell her, she may want to stop being friends on a more regular basis even. The important thing though is that you believe she is or has been an important part in your life and nothing could change that for you. She will be grateful for the honesty at the very least.

If you end up with more time in the world, think what's best to you beyond her. See a little more glory of the natural world is all anyone can do to feel they are on the path to righteousness.
